leonardo: In Annunciation, separated figures negotiate a legible architectural and landscape setting. Look at the interval between them before treating the episode as an isolated gesture.
Lady with an Ermine makes the turn of a body and the animal’s direction coordinate an encounter. The portrait’s animation differs from the earlier scene’s more distributed narrative attention.
Saint John the Baptist concentrates the exchange into a single emerging figure and directed gesture. This is a different economy of presence, not simply an increase in technical skill.
michelangelo: Doni Tondo compresses turning bodies into a circular field. The family group makes sculptural mass function inside a bounded painted surface.
The Creation of Adam carries a bodily contrast across a much larger architectural setting. Weight and approach matter as much as the famous fingers.
The Last Judgment makes many bodies contribute to a dense field of collective movement. Compare its crowded directional pressures with the more isolated encounter in the ceiling scene.
raphael: The Marriage of the Virgin organizes a narrative around a measured architectural axis. The people’s actions are legible within an insistently ordered space.
The Triumph of Galatea distributes movement through a mythological gathering. Rhythms of turning bodies establish another kind of coherence from the earlier architectural axis.
The Transfiguration brings sharply different conditions into one vertical arrangement. Consider how the upper and lower groups are joined without being made equivalent.
caravaggio: Bacchus constructs an encounter through the relation of a figure, offered object and near spectator. The apparently accessible surface should not be confused with an unposed event.
Basket of Fruit removes the human protagonist but retains a strong threshold between object and viewer. Material description carries an encounter usually assigned to a face or gesture.
The Entombment of Christ gives several bodies a shared downward action. Compare the pressure of the projecting edge with the offered objects in the earlier works.
rembrandt: The Anatomy Lesson organizes professional identity through demonstration and unequal access to the body. Different gazes make a commissioned group dynamic.
The Night Watch enlarges the problem of a collective portrait into an assembly that seems to act. Prominence is distributed through light and movement rather than an even row.

The Return of the Prodigal Son concentrates attention around touch and a relation between bodies. Its quieter center can be compared with the earlier works without turning a selective chronology into a biography of inevitable spiritual progress.
vermeer: The Milkmaid gives a repeated domestic action weight through light, mass and a concentrated hand-held task. The scene is intimate in scale without requiring knowledge of a private personality.
Woman Holding a Balance arrests a smaller action before an obvious outcome. Compare the space around the hand with the continuity implied by pouring in The Milkmaid.
The Lacemaker compresses activity further into a near field of concentrated attention. The change in scale and focus is a pictorial difference, not evidence that the artist rejected earlier concerns.
gentileschi: Susanna and the Elders organizes a body’s exposure to other people’s attention. The physical relation among figures can be examined before biographical analogy is introduced.

Judith Slaying Holofernes makes agency visible through coordinated force and the practical involvement of two women. Compare how action is distributed rather than reducing the image to one expression.

Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting gives a working body a professional and symbolic claim. The relation of artist, represented agent and public identity changes across these three very different subjects.
goya: The Parasol addresses leisure through an arranged relation of figures, shade and costume. Its apparent ease is a constructed social image.
The Third of May makes historical violence visible through opposed conditions of power and exposure. Compare the function of light with the earlier management of shade.

Saturn belongs to the Black Paintings, a different material and viewing history from a public commission or exhibition picture. Its disturbing bodily encounter should not be made into a universal key to all Goya’s earlier work.
turner: Dido Building Carthage gives a historical subject a substantial architectural setting. The scene’s light works through an intelligible arrangement of buildings, water and figures.
The Slave Ship makes visibility unstable within an intensely active sea. A historical subject is carried through a much less secure experience of spatial mastery.

Norham Castle, Sunrise reduces the insistence of solid boundaries as light becomes a principal organizing force. The selective sequence asks what remains recognizable when atmosphere takes greater authority.
monet: Women in the Garden coordinates sizeable figures with an outdoor setting. Light and shadow complicate the apparent stability of costume and pose.
Woman with a Parasol makes viewpoint and mobile handling reorganize a family encounter. Figures share their pictorial world with weather rather than stand apart from it.

San Giorgio Maggiore at Dusk makes architecture depend on atmospheric relationships and reflection. The changing balance of subject and perception connects these works without making them stages in a predetermined ascent.
morisot: The Harbor at Lorient locates a seated figure within a maritime view. Compare the person’s concentrated presence with the wider field of activity and distance.
Eugène Manet on the Isle of Wight makes a window shape what can be seen of another person’s attention. The barrier becomes a central pictorial relationship.
In the Dining Room gives an everyday interior authority through abbreviated handling. Across these works, social setting remains consequential even when boundaries become less insistently drawn.
van-gogh: The Potato Eaters gathers bodies and hands into a restricted field of light. Its earth colors and emphatic handling construct a particular image of labor and sustenance.
The Night Café uses converging space and charged color to make an interior difficult to inhabit comfortably. Recognizable objects become participants in an expressive arrangement.

Wheatfield with Crows distributes movement across paths, field and sky. Compare this less enclosed network of directions with the earlier interiors; do not treat the work as a documented final message.
cezanne: The Hanged Man’s House builds a landscape through dense material relationships. The place is recognizable, yet the paint’s organization remains insistent.
The Basket of Apples lets local alignments disturb a single continuous viewpoint. Objects remain weighty even when the supporting space cannot be effortlessly reconstructed.
The Large Bathers organizes bodies and landscape together at a different scale. The relationship between a figure and its surrounding structure becomes more important than narrative identification.
cassatt: Little Girl in a Blue Armchair makes an informal pose compete with expanses of upholstered furniture. Empty seating is an active part of the encounter.
The Boating Party uses large shapes and a forceful viewpoint to organize figures within a constrained space. A leisure subject becomes a demanding problem of proportion and address.

Young Mother Sewing concentrates attention around a task while a child establishes another relation to the spectator. Care and work remain specific activities rather than interchangeable emblems of domestic feeling.
kandinsky: The Blue Rider still offers a recognizable subject whose movement helps orient attention. Color and abbreviation already affect how securely that subject can be possessed.
Composition VIII distributes authority among geometric forms and open intervals. The eye has to establish routes without relying on a familiar depicted scene.
Several Circles reduces the vocabulary while retaining unequal visual weights, overlaps and distances. Fewer types of form do not imply a simpler experience of their relationships.
picasso: Five figures occupy a compressed interior. Faces do not share one descriptive language, and the angular planes make the surrounding space press forward rather than recede. The encounter concerns the viewer’s position as much as the represented bodies.

A figure reaches toward a reflection that does not simply repeat her. Curved divisions, saturated color and emphatic outlines turn resemblance into a negotiation between surface and imagined interior.
Two studies are represented; this is not a complete career chronology.
dali: A very small painting gives improbable objects the clarity of evidence. The landscape appears stable while the things used to measure time lose their resistance.
A crouched figure and a hand holding an egg share a contour. Seeing one form prepares the eye to discover another, making transformation an operation performed by the viewer.
Two studies are represented; this is not a complete career chronology.
pollock: The network is neither an illustration nor an undifferentiated accident. Dense crossings, suspended lines and exposed canvas produce an extended field in which attention keeps changing scale.
An extended web of marks holds open spaces within its movement. Rhythm emerges through uneven recurrence rather than through a repeated decorative unit.
Two studies are represented; this is not a complete career chronology.
matisse: Red joins the surfaces of a room without erasing every object inside it. The studio becomes an arrangement of intervals, outlines and paintings within the painting.
Five figures turn a ring into a precarious structure. The open handclasp and leaning bodies keep equilibrium visibly under negotiation.
Two studies are represented; this is not a complete career chronology.
kahlo: A seated figure, loose suit, scissors and scattered hair make appearance look deliberately made and unmade. An inscription complicates the relation between an image and the voice attributed to it.
Two seated self-images join hands while their exposed hearts remain connected. The double portrait makes identity relational, bodily and socially clothed.
Two studies are represented; this is not a complete career chronology.
magritte: An eye becomes a place where a sky appears. The image asks whether vision gives access to the world, constructs it, or becomes an object under another gaze.
A painted pipe and a sentence do not agree in the way a label usually promises. The encounter separates an object, its depiction and the language used to identify it.
Two studies are represented; this is not a complete career chronology.
